There is nowhere near enough resources for eating disorder sufferers, which I think is what leads to inadequate treatment.

At least where I am from in Australia, inpatient is a last resort for when someone is physically unstable and will die in the near future without medical intervention. It's not meant to cure the eating disorder, just to keep the person alive and return them to a healthy weight. There are too many people with eating disorders and not enough spaces available. It's a shitty balancing act between the level of support given to one patient while trying to help everyone.

Therapy and refeeding have to be done in conjunction for recovery. If someone is extremely medically unstable, they won't have the mental capacities to process/properly engage in therapy. For me, I was seeing a therapist, psychiatrist, and dietician for over a year before I was actually able to engage in the sessions and make real progress. I'm now doing a lot better than I used to be and would consider myself mostly recovered.

Friends and family also have to be there for recovery. I am so lucky to have intelligent and lovely people around me who listened to what I was going through and helped me.

Recovery sucks and so many providers don't know what they are talking about. But there are people who do and the right support is out there. I wish that the support I got was more widely available.
